name: Bitcoin
executive_summary: Bitcoin launched in 2009 as peer-to-peer electronic cash, and seventeen years later at the time of this scoring, that track record shows up in a TradFi score of 80: a fixed 21 million coin supply, deep access through ETFs and regulated custody, and more than 15 years of operation with a single exploited protocol bug, in 2010, reversed within hours. The AI score lands much lower at 54, because Bitcoin confirms transactions probabilistically rather than with an instant, guaranteed final settlement, and that's precisely the kind of certainty an autonomous agent needs before it can safely act on a payment. The 26-point gap between the two scores comes down to that one architectural choice: built for slow, battle-tested trust rather than machine-speed certainty.

key_findings: TradFi Approved is Bitcoin's strongest category at 97. Regulated ETFs, professional custody services, and licensed trading venues all exist at scale. US spot bitcoin ETFs held about $76.5 billion in November 2026 with cumulative net inflows of roughly $53.6 billion since launch, even after record outflows that month during a sharp price decline; no access point has closed.

Tokenomics & Supply scores 97, near the top of the scale. Bitcoin's 21 million coin cap is fixed and its issuance schedule, which cuts new supply in half on a predictable timer, is transparent and unchangeable. The score moved up from 95 because a large amount of Bitcoin mined in the network's earliest days, believed to belong to its pseudonymous creator, has been inactive for over fifteen years and is treated as dead capital rather than a live supply overhang -- those coins remain technically spendable, which is why the score stops short of a perfect 100.

On-Chain Health scores 85. The network handles roughly 550,000-600,000 transactions a day with about 750,000 daily active addresses in November 2026, but fees are historically low, around 0.6% of miner revenue, so miners rely almost entirely on the block subsidy. Hashrate dipped in mid-2026 as some public miners converted sites to AI data centers, then recovered to roughly 1,000 EH/s on a 30-day average.

Privacy & Confidentiality is a clear weak point at 36. Every Bitcoin transaction is permanently visible on a fully public ledger, with no built-in way to hide amounts or participants. Third-party mixing tools that once let users blend their coins with others' for extra privacy have thinned out significantly since several of the services that ran them shut down. Simply not disclosing which address belongs to you offers some privacy, but it's a personal habit, not a network protection, and specialized chain-analysis firms have repeatedly de-anonymized addresses in practice.

Decentralization scores 40. Roughly 36% of global Bitcoin mining hashrate sits in the United States by jurisdiction, and the three largest mining pools (Foundry, AntPool, F2Pool) together find about 64% of blocks. The jurisdiction risk is tempered by how slow and costly it would be for that hashrate to relocate: the 2021 China mining ban showed that kind of physical move takes months, not the near-instant switch a miner has between pools. That slower-moving risk is why the score is a calibrated discount rather than a straight mechanical read of the jurisdiction concentration alone.

Bitcoin's TradFi score of 80 sits at the boundary of the top tier, with about half a point of cushion. A drop of about three points in On-Chain Health or TradFi Approved alone, or four in Real-World Utility, would move Bitcoin to 79, just below the top band.

binding_cap.short_note: Capped by Deterministic Finality FAIL -- probabilistic-only PoW settlement, no deterministic finality mechanism.

key_findings: Bitcoin's AI score sits 26 points below its TradFi score, the widest gap between the two frameworks for this chain. The reason is structural: institutions trust Bitcoin deeply, but that trust was built on nearly two decades of slow, battle-tested settlement, not on the fast, mathematically guaranteed finality an autonomous agent needs before it can safely treat a payment as done.

Bitcoin fails our check for fast, guaranteed transaction finality outright, because it only ever confirms transactions probabilistically -- there's no point at which the network formally guarantees a transaction can never be reversed, only that reversal becomes increasingly unlikely over time. That failure caps Bitcoin's AI score at 54, just one point below the next tier up.

Security Posture is Bitcoin's strongest category on the AI framework at 88. The core protocol has run continuously for more than 15 years, and its one exploited protocol bug came in August 2010, when an overflow briefly created about 184 billion coins before a patched release and a chain rollback erased them within hours. Nothing comparable has happened since.

Agent Tooling scores 66. Lightning Labs' agent tools let AI agents pay over Lightning with narrowly scoped credentials, and a November 2026 release (pi402) lets a coding agent pay for AI inference per request. Production use beyond demos and early sellers remains limited. An August 2026 attack on merchant Lightning nodes exploited a flaw in BTCPay Server, a third-party payment server, that exposed node credentials; Lightning Labs' agent tools were not implicated.

watch_items: Quantum: two proposals, a quantum-resistant output type (BIP-360) and a plan to eventually retire vulnerable address types (BIP-361), remain drafts with no signature scheme chosen and no activation timeline. A November 2026 IOSCO report places a code-breaking quantum computer around 2030-2035, highly uncertain. Choosing a scheme and an activation path would be the trigger to revisit the quantum check.

Security budget: fees are about 0.6% of miner revenue, and some public miners are converting sites to AI data centers and selling bitcoin to fund it. If hashrate falls materially and stays down, or fees remain negligible as the block subsidy keeps halving, that bears on On-Chain Health and Security & Future-Proofing.

Programmability: CTV (BIP-119) has an activation client but effectively zero miner signaling, and OP_CAT (BIP-347) is a finished specification with no activation plan. Activation of either would raise how programmable Bitcoin can be scored.

Governance: an August 2026 soft fork pushed by a minority of node operators (BIP-110) failed with 2.5% miner signaling; its enforcing nodes split onto a chain that stalled after two blocks and later became a separate network, while the main chain was unaffected. A future contentious fork attempt with real miner or exchange support would be a re-check trigger.

Lightning: public channel capacity has fallen from its late-2025 high, though published figures disagree widely because large exchange channels are increasingly private. A clear, sustained decline in Lightning payment volume, or further exploits of widely used Lightning software, would bear on Real-World Utility and Agent Tooling.

Stablecoins on Bitcoin: USDT on Lightning (via Taproot Assets) is reported live since about March 2026 with no published usage, and USDT on RGB is set to launch on-chain in late November 2026. Material circulating supply would strengthen Real-World Utility.

There's no credible near-term path for Bitcoin to pass the fast-finality check. This isn't a maturity issue that more development time would fix; it's a fundamental result of how Bitcoin's proof-of-work settlement is designed.

tiles.cheapest_tx_cost_note: Market floor at roughly 0.2 sat/vB; many wallets default to a more conservative fee near 1 sat/vB (about $0.09).
